title: Planarian morphology behaves as a homeostatic parameter maintained toward a target shape

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planarian morphology behaves as a homeostatic parameter maintained toward a target shape

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: In planarians, morphology appears to be a homeostatic parameter that is repeatedly assessed and adjusted to maintain a 'target' morphology: after an incorrect head shape is produced during regeneration, the mismatch with the target triggers remodeling (between days 10 and 17 in octanol-treated G. dorotocephala), even after large-scale reorganization has ended.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M 2015, Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms › 3. Discussion › 3.5. Morphological Remodeling in 2 Phases: Head Shape Change without Traumatic Injury

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Morphology appears to be a homeostatic parameter, one that is consistently assessed and adjusted in order to maintain some “target” morphology.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Emmons-Bell M, Durant F, Hammelman J, Bessonov N, Volpert V, Morokuma J, Pinet K, Adams DS, Pietak A, Lobo D, Levin M, “Gap Junctional Blockade Stochastically Induces Different Species-Specific Head Anatomies in Genetically Wild-Type Girardia dorotocephala Flatworms”, International journal of molecular sciences (2015), doi:10.3390/ijms161126065; section “3. Discussion › 3.5. Morphological Remodeling in 2 Phases: Head Shape Change without Traumatic Injury”. Scope: Regenerating and remodeling planarians (G. dorotocephala)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2015-girardia-16: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing remodeling observations operationalize return to a set point in one perturbation. They do not uniquely identify error sensing or a homeostatic controller, so the stronger conceptual interpretation remains only partially testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify whether intact post-regeneration worms detect deviations and move morphology toward a stable species-specific set point without injury, including trajectories and stopping behavior. Compare feedback/set-point models against passive growth and turnover models.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Return toward normal shape does not uniquely demonstrate assessment of a target.

Complete longitudinal data are not clearly deposited.

Passive differential growth and tissue turnover are plausible rivals.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.4
data existence: 0.55
discriminating power: 0.45
operationalizability: 0.65
analysis feasibility: 0.75

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A setpoint is operationalized here as return toward species shape after a deviant regenerate, once large-scale regeneration has ended. The paper describes that return. The longitudinal measurements that would separate it from ongoing growth are not public, so the homeostatic reading cannot be resolved from existing records.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: After regeneration is complete, measure distance of each head to the species target over days 10 to 17 and test for a return that is absent in animals that already match the target. Return only from the mismatched heads would support a setpoint; indistinguishable drift in both groups would refute a distinct homeostatic correction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
The internal assessment step is not observed separately from the shape change.

Continued morphallaxis can move heads toward the species form without a repeated comparison to a target.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data adequacy: 0.28
discriminating power: 0.38
data existence: 0.3
operationalizability: 0.6
analysis feasibility: 0.3
